//! MINIX-style negative errno codes.
//!
//! Subset needed by Phase 2; more added as servers come online. Values match
//! MINIX 3 `include/minix/errno.h`. Returning a negative `m_type` is how an
//! IPC reply signals failure.

pub const OK: i32 = 0;
pub const EGENERIC: i32 = -1;
pub const EPERM: i32 = -2;
pub const ENOENT: i32 = -3;

pub const EINVAL: i32 = -21;
pub const EDEADLK: i32 = -29;
pub const ENOSYS: i32 = -44;

pub const EBADCALL: i32 = -102;
pub const EBADSRCDST: i32 = -103;
pub const ECALLDENIED: i32 = -104;
pub const EDEADSRCDST: i32 = -105;
pub const ENOTREADY: i32 = -106;
pub const EBADREQUEST: i32 = -107;
pub const ETRAPDENIED: i32 = -108;

            for &ipc in &[ELOCKED, EBADSRCDST, EDEADSRCDST, EDONTREPLY] {

    }
}

=== rminix errno.h ===
/* The <errno.h> header defines the numbers of the various errors that can
 * occur during program execution.  They are visible to user programs and 
 * should be small positive integers.  However, they are also used within 
 * MINIX, where they must be negative.  For example, the READ system call is 
 * executed internally by calling do_read().  This function returns either a 
 * (negative) error number or a (positive) number of bytes actually read.
 *
 * To solve the problem of having the error numbers be negative inside the
 * the system and positive outside, the following mechanism is used.  All the
 * definitions are are the form:
 *
 *	#define EPERM		(_SIGN 1)
 *
 * If the macro _SYSTEM is defined, then  _SIGN is set to "-", otherwise it is
 * set to "".  Thus when compiling the operating system, the  macro _SYSTEM
 * will be defined, setting EPERM to (- 1), whereas when when this
 * file is included in an ordinary user program, EPERM has the value ( 1).
 */

#ifndef _ERRNO_H		/* check if <errno.h> is already included */
#define _ERRNO_H		/* it is not included; note that fact */

/* Now define _SIGN as "" or "-" depending on _SYSTEM. */
#ifdef _SYSTEM
#   define _SIGN         -
#   define OK            0
#else
#   define _SIGN         
#endif

extern int errno;		  /* place where the error numbers go */

/* Here are the numerical values of the error numbers. */
#define _NERROR               70  /* number of errors */  

#define EGENERIC      (_SIGN 99)  /* generic error */
#define EPERM         (_SIGN  1)  /* operation not permitted */
#define ENOENT        (_SIGN  2)  /* no such file or directory */
#define ESRCH         (_SIGN  3)  /* no such process */

#define EBADF         (_SIGN  9)  /* bad file descriptor */

#define EAGAIN        (_SIGN 11)  /* resource temporarily unavailable */
#define ENOMEM        (_SIGN 12)  /* not enough space */
#define EACCES        (_SIGN 13)  /* permission denied */
#define EFAULT        (_SIGN 14)  /* bad address */
#define ENOTBLK       (_SIGN 15)  /* Extension: not a block special file */
#define EBUSY         (_SIGN 16)  /* resource busy */
#define EEXIST        (_SIGN 17)  /* file exists */
#define EXDEV         (_SIGN 18)  /* improper link */
#define ENODEV        (_SIGN 19)  /* no such device */
#define ENOTDIR       (_SIGN 20)  /* not a directory */
#define EISDIR        (_SIGN 21)  /* is a directory */

Design a detailed implementation plan for **slice 5.0** of the minix.rs project at /Users/kevinbarnard/src/minixrs. Read the files you need to verify details; do not write anything.

## What slice 5.0 is

Per `docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md` (read decisions **D7** and **D8**, and the "Slice 5.0" section), this slice does two mechanical, isolated things before any C exists:

1. **Renumber `kernel-shared/src/error.rs`** to classic-MINIX values (which are identical to Linux/musl for the POSIX block), with MINIX-specific IPC errnos moved to modern-MINIX's 200-band.
2. **Add a new host tool `tools/gen-c-headers`** (workspace member) that depends on `kernel-shared` and *prints* C headers generated from the live Rust constants — `minix/ipc.h`, `minix/com.h`, `minix/callnr.h`, plus errno values for `bits/errno.h` verification. Headers are generated at build time into the musl sysroot, **never committed**. CI must regenerate them and compile them with `clang -std=c11 -fsyntax-only` as a blocking host check.

## Decisions already locked (do not re-litigate)

- **POSIX block: the full contiguous 1–40 range** (classic MINIX == musl agree on all 40). Verified values: EPERM 1, ENOENT 2, ESRCH 3, EINTR 4, EIO 5, ENXIO 6, E2BIG 7, ENOEXEC 8, EBADF 9, ECHILD 10, EAGAIN 11, ENOMEM 12, EACCES 13, EFAULT 14, ENOTBLK 15, EBUSY 16, EEXIST 17, EXDEV 18, ENODEV 19, ENOTDIR 20, EISDIR 21, EINVAL 22, ENFILE 23, EMFILE 24, ENOTTY 25, ETXTBSY 26, EFBIG 27, ENOSPC 28, ESPIPE 29, EROFS 30, EMLINK 31, EPIPE 32, EDOM 33, ERANGE 34, EDEADLK 35, ENAMETOOLONG 36, ENOLCK 37, ENOSYS 38, ENOTEMPTY 39, ELOOP 40. Constants stay **negated** in Rust (`pub const EPERM: i32 = -1;`) as today.
- **MINIX-specific band, values taken from modern MINIX 3's `sys/sys/errno.h`:** ENOTREADY 201, EDEADSRCDST 202, EDONTREPLY 203, EGENERIC 204, ELOCKED 208, EBADCALL 209, ECALLDENIED 210, ETRAPDENIED 211, EBADREQUEST 212. The one existing name modern MINIX lacks is **EBADSRCDST** — modern MINIX spells the same condition `EBADEPT` = 216, so EBADSRCDST takes **216** with a comment noting the modern spelling. (Reserved-but-unused modern values in that band: ERESTART 200, EPACKSIZE 205, EURG 206, ENOURG 207, EBADMODE 213, ENOCONN 214, EDEADEPT 215, EBADCPU 217 — do not add them.)
- **`error.rs` uses a small declarative macro** that takes the positive musl value and emits both the negated `pub const` and a derived `pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)]` name/value table. Doc comments on each entry must still work (`$(#[$m:meta])*`). The table is the single source of truth consumed by the header generator and by the host tests.
- **Crate name `minixrs-gen-c-headers`**, directory `tools/gen-c-headers/`. Add a `.cargo/config.toml` alias so `cargo gen-c-headers` works, and correct the plan doc's `cargo run -p gen-c-headers` line.

## Verified facts about the repo (from prior exploration — trust these, spot-check only if a design choice depends on it)

- `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` is 97 lines: 28 bare `pub const i32` + 3 tests. It is the workspace's ONLY errno definition site.
- **There are ZERO hardcoded numeric errno literals anywhere in the workspace** (code, asm, host tests, `tests/qemu-boot.expected`, `tests/qemu-boot.forbidden`). Every negative integer literal in the tree is a ProcNr, not an errno. So marker churn is zero and no consumer code needs a value fix.

# Slice 5.0 — errno renumber (D7) + `tools/gen-c-headers` (D8)

## Context

Phase 4 is complete and the pre-Phase-5 cleanup has landed (chunk 6, PR #39, merged
2026-07-24 — `8deaa39`). Phase 5 brings a musl fork and real filesystems, and its
first slice is deliberately **ABI prep before any C exists**:

1. `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` currently carries **bespoke** errno values
   (`EINVAL = -21`, `EFAULT = -15`, `ENOSYS = -44`) behind a comment that wrongly
   claims they "match MINIX 3". musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and its
   `syscall_ret.c` `r > -4096UL` convention only work unmodified if minix.rs
   adopts musl's numbering. Renumbering **now** means no later Phase 5 slice ever
   bakes a soon-to-change errno into a trace marker or a line of C — slice 5.1's
   proof bar already cites `result=-14` (`EFAULT` at its final value).
2. The musl fork needs C headers describing the minix.rs ABI. D8 rejects cbindgen
   (it cannot const-eval the `ProcNr::new()` endpoint constants) in favour of a
   hand-rolled host tool that reads the live Rust constants and prints C. Headers
   are **generated at build time, never committed**, so drift is impossible by
   construction. The ABI freezes at slice 5.6.

Outcome: after this slice the ABI is C-ready, and CI proves the generated headers
compile as C11 on every PR.

Branch: `feature/slice-5.0-abi-prep`. One PR.

---

## Part 1 — `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` rewrite

**Replace the whole file in one write.** `EACCES` is `-14` today and `EFAULT`
becomes `-14`; any incremental edit passes through a state where two live names
alias.

### Shape (decided)

A private declarative macro takes the **positive** musl magnitude and emits both
the negated `pub const` and a derived name/value table:

```rust
macro_rules! errnos {
    ($( $(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident = $magnitude:literal, )*) => {
        $( $(#[$meta])* pub const $name: i32 = -$magnitude; )*
        /// Every errno as `(name, value)` pairs, POSIX block then MINIX band.
        /// Single source of truth for `tools/gen-c-headers`, the band guards,
        /// and the host tests. A `const` (not a `static`) so the kernel — which
        /// never references it — pays nothing in `.rodata`.
        pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)] = &[ $( (stringify!($name), $name), )* ];
    };
}
```

`$(#[$meta:meta])*` captures `///` docs (they desugar to `#[doc]` before matching),
so per-entry rustdoc still works. `$magnitude:literal` (not `:expr`) keeps
`-$magnitude` unambiguous.

### Values

- **POSIX block, magnitudes 1..=40, contiguous** — verified byte-identical between
  `/Users/kevinbarnard/src/learn/rminix/include/errno.h` (classic MINIX) and
  musl's `arch/generic/bits/errno.h`: EPERM 1, ENOENT 2, ESRCH 3, EINTR 4, EIO 5,
  ENXIO 6, E2BIG 7, ENOEXEC 8, EBADF 9, ECHILD 10, EAGAIN 11, ENOMEM 12, EACCES 13,
  EFAULT 14, ENOTBLK 15, EBUSY 16, EEXIST 17, EXDEV 18, ENODEV 19, ENOTDIR 20,
  EISDIR 21, EINVAL 22, ENFILE 23, EMFILE 24, ENOTTY 25, ETXTBSY 26, EFBIG 27,
  ENOSPC 28, ESPIPE 29, EROFS 30, EMLINK 31, EPIPE 32, EDOM 33, ERANGE 34,
  EDEADLK 35, ENAMETOOLONG 36, ENOLCK 37, ENOSYS 38, ENOTEMPTY 39, ELOOP 40.
- **MINIX band, from modern MINIX 3's `sys/sys/errno.h`** — ENOTREADY 201,
  EDEADSRCDST 202, EDONTREPLY 203, EGENERIC 204, ELOCKED 208, EBADCALL 209,
  ECALLDENIED 210, ETRAPDENIED 211, EBADREQUEST 212, and **EBADSRCDST 216** (the
  one name modern MINIX lacks — it spells that condition `EBADEPT` = 216; keep the
  classic name at the modern value and say so in a doc comment).
- Record in the module docs the reserved-but-unadopted 200-band values so nobody
  reuses them: ERESTART 200, EPACKSIZE 205, EURG 206, ENOURG 207, EBADMODE 213,
  ENOCONN 214, EDEADEPT 215, EBADCPU 217.
- `OK = 0` stays, outside `ALL`. Add `POSIX_ERRNO_MAX = 40` and
  `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE = 200`.
- Module doc replaces the wrong "matches MINIX 3" claim with the actual D7 policy.

### Compile-time guards (house `const _: () = …` idiom)

Enforce D7's invariant so nothing can ever land in the 41..=199 gap — the range
where musl defines errnos minix.rs has *not* adopted:

- every value negative; POSIX magnitudes cover 1..=40 exactly once with no holes;
  every other magnitude `>= MINIX_ERRNO_BASE`;
- all values pairwise distinct;
- `OK == 0` (nine sites still spell success as `sef.receive(…) != 0`);
- `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE > POSIX_ERRNO_MAX`.

Const-eval constraints on the pinned nightly: **no iterators/`for`** (use `while` +
`ALL[i]` + `<[T]>::len()`), and **`assert!` messages must be literals** (`assert_eq!`
and `assert!(c, "{x}")` are rejected in const). If slice-indexing `ALL` in a const
block gives trouble, fall back to a `const fn check(t: &[(&str, i32)]) -> ()`.

### Tests

Keep `ok_is_zero`. Drop `ipc_errors_distinct_from_posix_errors` (subsumed).
Add, all driven off `ALL`: `all_errors_are_negative`, `all_values_distinct`,
`posix_block_matches_musl` (against a literally-pinned 40-entry table — the drift
tripwire, so a renumber must be a deliberate two-place edit),
`minix_band_matches_modern_minix`, `minix_band_clear_of_musl_range`, and
`table_names_resolve_to_the_named_constants` (proves the macro paired
`stringify!($name)` with the right constant — invisible to every other test).

Use `assert_eq!`, never bare `assert!(CONST op CONST)` inside a `#[test]` — that
trips `assertions_on_constants` under `--all-targets -D warnings`.

### Consumer sweep: zero code changes

Verified: all 27 import sites are symbolic; the only fully-qualified reference is
`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:71` (`minixrs_kernel_shared::error::EINVAL`), still
symbolic. There are **no hardcoded numeric errno literals anywhere** — every
negative literal in the tree is a ProcNr. `tests/qemu-boot.expected` /
`.forbidden` carry no errno values, so marker churn is zero. `kernel/build.rs`
already watches `kernel-shared/src` recursively, so the nested server ELFs rebuild.

**Do not** drive-by the nine `sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0` → `!= OK` sites: they
touch five server `main.rs` files and would force a QEMU re-verify for no ABI
reason. Nominate for 5.1, which already owns `server-rt`.

---

## Part 2 — `tools/gen-c-headers` (package `minixrs-gen-c-headers`)

First Rust crate under `tools/` and the first host/`std` crate in the workspace.
Lib + thin bin, matching the `servers/ds` shape (`registry.rs` measured,
`main.rs` Sonar-excluded):

```
tools/gen-c-headers/
  Cargo.toml            # literal fields, publish = false, [lib] + [[bin]], zero third-party deps
  src/lib.rs            # #![forbid(unsafe_code)], artifact list, cross-artifact tests
      builder.rs        # CFile writer: banner, guards, #define, _Static_assert
      ipc_h.rs  com_h.rs  callnr_h.rs  errno_h.rs  selftest.rs
      main.rs           # argv + fs I/O only
```

`publish = false` is load-bearing (`release.yml` publishes a hardcoded 5-crate
list). Zero third-party deps keeps `deny.toml`'s license allow-list untouched.

### CLI

`cargo gen-c-headers [OUTDIR]` (default `target/gen-c-headers`), `--stdout` to
concatenate every artifact to stdout (D8's literal "*prints* the headers"; the
eyeball path), `--help`. `main()` returns `ExitCode`. **Determinism rule, stated in
the crate docs:** no timestamps, hostnames, absolute paths or env reads in output —
the same commit must produce byte-identical bytes for the 5.6 sysroot cache.

Output tree:

```
target/gen-c-headers/
  include/minix/{ipc.h, com.h, callnr.h, errno.h}
  abi-check/errno.h      # musl stand-in, CI-only
  abi-selftest.c
```

`tools/build-musl.sh` (5.6) will copy `include/minix` into the sysroot.

### `builder.rs`

Append-only `CFile { out: String }` with `new(title, sources)` (SPDX + copyright +
`GENERATED FILE -- DO NOT EDIT` banner naming the source `.rs` files and
`cargo gen-c-headers`), `guard_open/close`, `section`, `block_comment`, `include`,
`define_dec`, `define_hex`, `define_ep`, `static_assert`, `finish`. Two rules that
get their own tests: `define_dec` must parenthesize negatives (`(-2)`, or
`x-SYSTEM_PROC_NR` mis-parses), and all output must stay **ASCII** (no em dashes
leaking into a header that ships into musl).

Use `push_str` + `format!("{name}")`; not `fmt::Write` (`write!` into a `String`
returns a `Result` clippy makes you handle) and never `format!("{}", x)`
(`uninlined_format_args` is default-on).

### `minix/ipc.h`

C11 **keywords**, not GNU attributes: `_Alignas` / `_Alignof` / `_Static_assert`
are guaranteed under `-std=c11 -pedantic-errors`; `__attribute__((aligned))` is not.
Only include is `<stddef.h>` for `offsetof` (a freestanding header, C11 §4p6, so it
survives `-nostdlibinc`).

- `typedef int endpoint_t;` + `_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, …)`.
- `ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT 15`, `ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK 0x7fff`,
  `ENDPOINT_MAX_GENERATION 65535`, `ENDPOINT_SLOT_TOP 16383`.
- `_ENDPOINT(g,p)` / `_ENDPOINT_G(e)` / `_ENDPOINT_P(e)` mirroring
  `endpoint.rs`, including the **sign-extension from bit 14** (minix.rs's
  deliberate deviation from MINIX 3's offset bias) — documented in a block comment.
- `struct message` with `_Alignas(8)` on the **first member** (C11 forbids an
  alignment specifier on a struct type declaration; member alignment yields
  `_Alignof(message) == 8`), then `_Static_assert`s pinning sizeof 104, alignof 8,
  and the three member offsets — every number `format!`ed from
  `size_of::<Message>()` / `align_of::<Message>()` / live pointer arithmetic,
  **never typed in**.
- IPC primitives SEND..NOTIFY_MESSAGE.
- Emits **no claim about which register carries the primitive number** —
  `ipc_const.rs:3`'s "`r1`/`x16`" is wrong (it is `x1`), and the plan assigns that
  fix to 5.1; cite the module instead of repeating the claim.

### `minix/com.h`

Includes `<minix/ipc.h>`. `NR_TASKS/NR_PROCS/NR_SYS_PROCS/NR_BOOT_PROCS`,
`ANY/NONE/SELF` cast to `endpoint_t`, `OK`, `EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR`.

Every process gets **two** macros with a block comment explaining they are not
interchangeable: `<NAME>_PROC_NR` (table slot, negative for tasks) and
`<NAME>_EP` (boot endpoint — what belongs in an IPC call). They differ for tasks
because of the sign-extension. `_EP` values come from calling `com::boot_endpoint(nr)`
in the generator (no such Rust const exists; deriving it is exactly the tool's job).
Then `_Static_assert`s validating the hand-written C decode against the
Rust-computed constants — the best value-per-line in the slice:

```c
_Static_assert(SYSTEM_EP == _ENDPOINT(0, SYSTEM_PROC_NR), "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(SYSTEM_EP) == SYSTEM_PROC_NR,  "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(HARDWARE_EP) == HARDWARE_PROC_NR, "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(PM_EP) == PM_PROC_NR, "…");
```

Deliberate omissions, each with a one-line comment so the choice is visible:
stub proc-nrs (`boot-stubs`-scoped, no C consumer), `NR_SERVED_PROCS`,
`USER_VA_TOP`, `sys_limits::*`, and signal numbers (musl's `<signal.h>` is
authoritative and already agrees).

### `minix/callnr.h`

`KERNEL_CALL 0x600` + `SYS_GETINFO`..`SYS_ENDKSIG` (0x600–0x611); `NR_SYS_CALLS 32`;
`GET_WHOAMI`, `SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN`, `EXEC_NAME_LEN`, `PRIVCTL_SET_USER`,
`SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL`, the `VMCTL_*` subcalls + prot flags; the five bands
(PM 0x700, VM 0xC00, SEF 0xD00, DS 0xE00, SCHED 0xF00) with their members and
counts; `_Static_assert`s mirroring the Rust `const _` ordering guards.

Two banner notes: (a) MINIX 3's `callnr.h` holds POSIX syscall numbers while ours
holds kernel-call + server-request numbers — a documented deviation; (b)
`NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` is emitted as **`NR_KERN_CALLS`** with a
`/* kernel-shared: NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 */` provenance comment (renaming the Rust
const is nominated for 5.1 — it must be settled before the 5.6 freeze).
**Payload byte offsets are not emitted in 5.0** — they exist only as Rust doc
comments, and D8 says the headers grow as later slices add bands; say so in a
comment, with 5.6's first musl wrapper as the forcing function.

### `minix/errno.h` + the guarded POSIX check

The real hole in "compile it in CI": there is no musl sysroot in 5.0, and a host
`<errno.h>` has **different** values (Darwin `EDEADLK` is 11, `EAGAIN` 35), so
asserting against it would be wrong — or, on glibc, right for the wrong reason.
Three parts:

1. `minix/errno.h` defines **only the MINIX 200-band** (positive magnitudes,
   `<errno.h>` convention; the wire carries them negated) plus always-on
   `_Static_assert(X >= 200)` band guards. The POSIX block is deliberately *not*
   defined — it comes from the C library, which is the whole point of D7.
2. An **opt-in** verification block:
   `#ifdef MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO` → `#include <errno.h>` → 40
   `_Static_assert(EPERM == 1, …)` generated from `error::ALL`. `tools/build-musl.sh`
   (5.6) defines the macro so these fire against the fork's real `bits/errno.h`.
3. A generated **stand-in** `abi-check/errno.h` (40 `#define`s at musl's values from
   the same Rust table, loud "NOT A REAL LIBC HEADER" banner, never installed into
   a sysroot) so CI compiles the guarded block from day one — otherwise a typo like
   `EDEALDK` sits undetected for six slices. Be honest in the plan doc: in 5.0 this
   is a **syntax and name-spelling check**; the value check lands in 5.6.

### `abi-selftest.c`

A header is never a translation unit, so its `_Static_assert`s never fire and
`-fsyntax-only` has nothing to chew on. The selftest is what makes the gate real:
include all four headers **twice** (proves the guards guard), add cross-header
invariants no single header can express (`SCHED_RQ_BASE + NR_SCHED_MSGS - 1 <
NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, `PM_RQ_BASE > KERNEL_CALL + NR_KERN_CALLS - 1`, sentinel
distinctness), and end with a file-scope typedef (ISO C forbids an empty TU).

---

## Part 3 — Host tests for the generator

In-module `#[cfg(test)]` (house style; no crate has a `tests/` dir), inside the
measured lib modules.

**D8's mandated layout snapshot** (`ipc_h.rs`) — asserts the *generated text*
contains `sizeof(message) == {size_of::<Message>()}`, `_Alignof(message) ==
{align_of::<Message>()}` and the payload offset computed by live pointer
arithmetic, plus pins 104/8 directly. This is what stops the generator hardcoding
the numbers and makes a Rust layout change surface in the header or fail here.

Plus: `com_h` — `_EP` values equal `boot_endpoint(nr)` recomputed in the test,
negative proc-nrs parenthesized, every process has both macros. `callnr_h` — call
numbers and band bases render from the live constants. `errno_h` — MINIX band is
`error::ALL` above the base, POSIX block is asserted-not-defined, stand-in covers
exactly the 40. `builder` — writer mechanics. `lib` (cross-artifact) — SPDX +
DO-NOT-EDIT on every artifact, all-ASCII, header guards unique, no duplicate
`#define` names within a header, all define names are C identifiers, artifact
paths relative and distinct, and rendering is deterministic.

---

## Part 4 — CI

New **blocking** job `c-headers` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after
`clippy-kernel`, using the house host skeleton verbatim (checkout
`@df4cb1c0…# v6.0.3` → `run: rustup show` → `Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b4977…# v2`):

1. `cargo gen-c-headers`
2. `clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only
   -nostdlibinc -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c`,
   run for both the host triple and `--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`
3. the same with `-DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO -Itarget/gen-c-headers/abi-check`
4. `git diff --exit-code && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` — D8's
   never-committed rule, made mechanical

`-nostdlibinc` (not `-nostdinc`) keeps it hermetic while preserving clang's
freestanding resource-dir headers, so the selftest can only see the generated
headers and cannot accidentally validate against the host libc. No clang install
step: `kernel/build.rs` already shells out to bare `clang`, so it is an existing
hard requirement. Every non-obvious choice gets a `#` comment, per house style.

No other job needs changing: `fmt`/`clippy`/`geiger`/`coverage` pick the member up
automatically, `audit`/`deny` see no new deps, `qemu-smoke` markers are unchanged,
and the crate stays off `miri`'s list deliberately (`forbid(unsafe_code)`, pure
`String` building, all FS I/O in `main.rs`).

---

## Part 5 — Config and docs

- **`Cargo.toml`** — add `"tools/gen-c-headers"` to `members`.
- **`.cargo/config.toml`** — `gen-c-headers = "run -p minixrs-gen-c-headers --"`
  with a comment on the never-committed output.
- **`sonar-project.properties`** — add `tools/**/src/main.rs` to
  `sonar.coverage.exclusions` plus a fourth bullet in the existing rationale block
  (host build-tool entry point: argv + file writes, content produced and unit-tested
  in the measured lib modules, end-to-end verified by the `c-headers` job).
- **`docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`** — 5.0 heading → `◀ ready (branch
  feature/slice-5.0-abi-prep, pending merge)`, 5.1 heading → `◀ next`; fix the
  proof line's `cargo run -p gen-c-headers` → `cargo gen-c-headers`; record the
  5.0 errno-check deferral (POSIX values verified against musl only from 5.6).
- **`docs/plan.md`** — same two marker flips; retitle the pre-Phase-5 section
  `(complete)` and flip chunk 6 to `✓ shipped (PR #39, merged 2026-07-24)`.
- **`docs/plans/phase-5-prep.md:143`** — same chunk-6 flip (currently still
  `◀ ready (branch feature/phase-5-plan, pending merge)`, but `8deaa39` merged it).
- **`docs/plans/phase-2-ipc.md:19`** — additive note on the stale "MINIX errno
  values" claim (it is a history file; annotate, don't rewrite).
- **`book/src/build.md:184`** — "Ten jobs" → "Eleven jobs", add the `c-headers`
  row; add `cargo gen-c-headers` / `cargo test -p minixrs-gen-c-headers` to the
  host-test section. `book/src/reference/syscalls.md` — short "Generated C headers"
  subsection. `book/src/reference/minix3-mapping.md` — correct the `error codes`
  row's provenance and note the headers are generated back into C. No new chapter
  in 5.0 — revisit at 5.6.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — "Nine gates" → "Ten gates", `c-headers` added to the blocking
  list ("the other **eight** block"); `cargo gen-c-headers` in the build section;
  one new conventions bullet covering the two-band errno policy + `errnos!` macro +
  `ALL` as single source of truth, the generator's lib+bin shape and

## Verification

```sh
cargo fmt --all && cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Slice 5.0 — errno renumber (D7) + `tools/gen-c-headers` (D8)

## Context

Phase 4 is complete and the pre-Phase-5 cleanup has landed (chunk 6, PR #39, merged
2026-07-24 — `8deaa39`). Phase 5 brings a musl fork and real filesystems, and its
first slice is deliberately **ABI prep before any C exists**:

1. `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` currently carries **bespoke** errno values
   (`EINVAL = -21`, `EFAULT = -15`, `ENOSYS = -44`) behind a comment that wrongly
   claims they "match MINIX 3". musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and its
   `syscall_ret.c` `r > -4096UL` convention only work unmodified if minix.rs
   adopts musl's numbering. Renumbering **now** means no later Phase 5 slice ever
   bakes a soon-to-change errno into a trace marker or a line of C — slice 5.1's
   proof bar already cites `result=-14` (`EFAULT` at its final value).
2. The musl fork needs C headers describing the minix.rs ABI. D8 rejects cbindgen
   (it cannot const-eval the `ProcNr::new()` endpoint constants) in favour of a
   hand-rolled host tool that reads the live Rust constants and prints C. Headers
   are **generated at build time, never committed**, so drift is impossible by
   construction. The ABI freezes at slice 5.6.

Outcome: after this slice the ABI is C-ready, and CI proves the generated headers
compile as C11 on every PR.

Branch: `feature/slice-5.0-abi-prep`. One PR.

---

## Part 1 — `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` rewrite

**Replace the whole file in one write.** `EACCES` is `-14` today and `EFAULT`
becomes `-14`; any incremental edit passes through a state where two live names
alias.

### Shape (decided)

A private declarative macro takes the **positive** musl magnitude and emits both
the negated `pub const` and a derived name/value table:

```rust
macro_rules! errnos {
    ($( $(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident = $magnitude:literal, )*) => {
        $( $(#[$meta])* pub const $name: i32 = -$magnitude; )*
        /// Every errno as `(name, value)` pairs, POSIX block then MINIX band.
        /// Single source of truth for `tools/gen-c-headers`, the band guards,
        /// and the host tests. A `const` (not a `static`) so the kernel — which
        /// never references it — pays nothing in `.rodata`.
        pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)] = &[ $( (stringify!($name), $name), )* ];
    };
}
```

`$(#[$meta:meta])*` captures `///` docs (they desugar to `#[doc]` before matching),
so per-entry rustdoc still works. `$magnitude:literal` (not `:expr`) keeps
`-$magnitude` unambiguous.

### Values

- **POSIX block, magnitudes 1..=40, contiguous** — verified byte-identical between
  `/Users/kevinbarnard/src/learn/rminix/include/errno.h` (classic MINIX) and
  musl's `arch/generic/bits/errno.h`: EPERM 1, ENOENT 2, ESRCH 3, EINTR 4, EIO 5,
  ENXIO 6, E2BIG 7, ENOEXEC 8, EBADF 9, ECHILD 10, EAGAIN 11, ENOMEM 12, EACCES 13,
  EFAULT 14, ENOTBLK 15, EBUSY 16, EEXIST 17, EXDEV 18, ENODEV 19, ENOTDIR 20,
  EISDIR 21, EINVAL 22, ENFILE 23, EMFILE 24, ENOTTY 25, ETXTBSY 26, EFBIG 27,
  ENOSPC 28, ESPIPE 29, EROFS 30, EMLINK 31, EPIPE 32, EDOM 33, ERANGE 34,
  EDEADLK 35, ENAMETOOLONG 36, ENOLCK 37, ENOSYS 38, ENOTEMPTY 39, ELOOP 40.
- **MINIX band, from modern MINIX 3's `sys/sys/errno.h`** — ENOTREADY 201,
  EDEADSRCDST 202, EDONTREPLY 203, EGENERIC 204, ELOCKED 208, EBADCALL 209,
  ECALLDENIED 210, ETRAPDENIED 211, EBADREQUEST 212, and **EBADSRCDST 216** (the
  one name modern MINIX lacks — it spells that condition `EBADEPT` = 216; keep the
  classic name at the modern value and say so in a doc comment).
- Record in the module docs the reserved-but-unadopted 200-band values so nobody
  reuses them: ERESTART 200, EPACKSIZE 205, EURG 206, ENOURG 207, EBADMODE 213,
  ENOCONN 214, EDEADEPT 215, EBADCPU 217.
- `OK = 0` stays, outside `ALL`. Add `POSIX_ERRNO_MAX = 40` and
  `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE = 200`.
- Module doc replaces the wrong "matches MINIX 3" claim with the actual D7 policy.

### Compile-time guards (house `const _: () = …` idiom)

Enforce D7's invariant so nothing can ever land in the 41..=199 gap — the range
where musl defines errnos minix.rs has *not* adopted:

- every value negative; POSIX magnitudes cover 1..=40 exactly once with no holes;
  every other magnitude `>= MINIX_ERRNO_BASE`;
- all values pairwise distinct;
- `OK == 0` (nine sites still spell success as `sef.receive(…) != 0`);
- `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE > POSIX_ERRNO_MAX`.

Const-eval constraints on the pinned nightly: **no iterators/`for`** (use `while` +
`ALL[i]` + `<[T]>::len()`), and **`assert!` messages must be literals** (`assert_eq!`
and `assert!(c, "{x}")` are rejected in const). If slice-indexing `ALL` in a const
block gives trouble, fall back to a `const fn check(t: &[(&str, i32)]) -> ()`.

### Tests

Keep `ok_is_zero`. Drop `ipc_errors_distinct_from_posix_errors` (subsumed).
Add, all driven off `ALL`: `all_errors_are_negative`, `all_values_distinct`,
`posix_block_matches_musl` (against a literally-pinned 40-entry table — the drift
tripwire, so a renumber must be a deliberate two-place edit),
`minix_band_matches_modern_minix`, `minix_band_clear_of_musl_range`, and
`table_names_resolve_to_the_named_constants` (proves the macro paired
`stringify!($name)` with the right constant — invisible to every other test).

Use `assert_eq!`, never bare `assert!(CONST op CONST)` inside a `#[test]` — that
trips `assertions_on_constants` under `--all-targets -D warnings`.

### Consumer sweep: zero code changes

Verified: all 27 import sites are symbolic; the only fully-qualified reference is
`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:71` (`minixrs_kernel_shared::error::EINVAL`), still
symbolic. There are **no hardcoded numeric errno literals anywhere** — every
negative literal in the tree is a ProcNr. `tests/qemu-boot.expected` /
`.forbidden` carry no errno values, so marker churn is zero. `kernel/build.rs`
already watches `kernel-shared/src` recursively, so the nested server ELFs rebuild.

**Do not** drive-by the nine `sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0` → `!= OK` sites: they
touch five server `main.rs` files and would force a QEMU re-verify for no ABI
reason. Nominate for 5.1, which already owns `server-rt`.

---

## Part 2 — `tools/gen-c-headers` (package `minixrs-gen-c-headers`)

First Rust crate under `tools/` and the first host/`std` crate in the workspace.
Lib + thin bin, matching the `servers/ds` shape (`registry.rs` measured,
`main.rs` Sonar-excluded):

```
tools/gen-c-headers/
  Cargo.toml            # literal fields, publish = false, [lib] + [[bin]], zero third-party deps
  src/lib.rs            # #![forbid(unsafe_code)], artifact list, cross-artifact tests
      builder.rs        # CFile writer: banner, guards, #define, _Static_assert
      ipc_h.rs  com_h.rs  callnr_h.rs  errno_h.rs  selftest.rs
      main.rs           # argv + fs I/O only
```

`publish = false` is load-bearing (`release.yml` publishes a hardcoded 5-crate
list). Zero third-party deps keeps `deny.toml`'s license allow-list untouched.

### CLI

`cargo gen-c-headers [OUTDIR]` (default `target/gen-c-headers`), `--stdout` to
concatenate every artifact to stdout (D8's literal "*prints* the headers"; the
eyeball path), `--help`. `main()` returns `ExitCode`. **Determinism rule, stated in
the crate docs:** no timestamps, hostnames, absolute paths or env reads in output —
the same commit must produce byte-identical bytes for the 5.6 sysroot cache.

Output tree:

```
target/gen-c-headers/
  include/minix/{ipc.h, com.h, callnr.h, errno.h}
  abi-check/errno.h      # musl stand-in, CI-only
  abi-selftest.c
```

`tools/build-musl.sh` (5.6) will copy `include/minix` into the sysroot.

### `builder.rs`

Append-only `CFile { out: String }` with `new(title, sources)` (SPDX + copyright +
`GENERATED FILE -- DO NOT EDIT` banner naming the source `.rs` files and
`cargo gen-c-headers`), `guard_open/close`, `section`, `block_comment`, `include`,
`define_dec`, `define_hex`, `define_ep`, `static_assert`, `finish`. Two rules that
get their own tests: `define_dec` must parenthesize negatives (`(-2)`, or
`x-SYSTEM_PROC_NR` mis-parses), and all output must stay **ASCII** (no em dashes
leaking into a header that ships into musl).

Use `push_str` + `format!("{name}")`; not `fmt::Write` (`write!` into a `String`
returns a `Result` clippy makes you handle) and never `format!("{}", x)`
(`uninlined_format_args` is default-on).

### `minix/ipc.h`

C11 **keywords**, not GNU attributes: `_Alignas` / `_Alignof` / `_Static_assert`
are guaranteed under `-std=c11 -pedantic-errors`; `__attribute__((aligned))` is not.
Only include is `<stddef.h>` for `offsetof` (a freestanding header, C11 §4p6, so it
survives `-nostdlibinc`).

- `typedef int endpoint_t;` + `_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, …)`.
- `ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT 15`, `ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK 0x7fff`,
  `ENDPOINT_MAX_GENERATION 65535`, `ENDPOINT_SLOT_TOP 16383`.
- `_ENDPOINT(g,p)` / `_ENDPOINT_G(e)` / `_ENDPOINT_P(e)` mirroring
  `endpoint.rs`, including the **sign-extension from bit 14** (minix.rs's
  deliberate deviation from MINIX 3's offset bias) — documented in a block comment.
- `struct message` with `_Alignas(8)` on the **first member** (C11 forbids an
  alignment specifier on a struct type declaration; member alignment yields
  `_Alignof(message) == 8`), then `_Static_assert`s pinning sizeof 104, alignof 8,
  and the three member offsets — every number `format!`ed from
  `size_of::<Message>()` / `align_of::<Message>()` / live pointer arithmetic,
  **never typed in**.
- IPC primitives SEND..NOTIFY_MESSAGE.
- Emits **no claim about which register carries the primitive number** —
  `ipc_const.rs:3`'s "`r1`/`x16`" is wrong (it is `x1`), and the plan assigns that
  fix to 5.1; cite the module instead of repeating the claim.

### `minix/com.h`

Includes `<minix/ipc.h>`. `NR_TASKS/NR_PROCS/NR_SYS_PROCS/NR_BOOT_PROCS`,
`ANY/NONE/SELF` cast to `endpoint_t`, `OK`, `EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR`.

Every process gets **two** macros with a block comment explaining they are not
interchangeable: `<NAME>_PROC_NR` (table slot, negative for tasks) and
`<NAME>_EP` (boot endpoint — what belongs in an IPC call). They differ for tasks
because of the sign-extension. `_EP` values come from calling `com::boot_endpoint(nr)`
in the generator (no such Rust const exists; deriving it is exactly the tool's job).
Then `_Static_assert`s validating the hand-written C decode against the
Rust-computed constants — the best value-per-line in the slice:

```c
_Static_assert(SYSTEM_EP == _ENDPOINT(0, SYSTEM_PROC_NR), "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(SYSTEM_EP) == SYSTEM_PROC_NR,  "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(HARDWARE_EP) == HARDWARE_PROC_NR, "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(PM_EP) == PM_PROC_NR, "…");
```

Deliberate omissions, each with a one-line comment so the choice is visible:
stub proc-nrs (`boot-stubs`-scoped, no C consumer), `NR_SERVED_PROCS`,
`USER_VA_TOP`, `sys_limits::*`, and signal numbers (musl's `<signal.h>` is
authoritative and already agrees).

### `minix/callnr.h`

`KERNEL_CALL 0x600` + `SYS_GETINFO`..`SYS_ENDKSIG` (0x600–0x611); `NR_SYS_CALLS 32`;
`GET_WHOAMI`, `SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN`, `EXEC_NAME_LEN`, `PRIVCTL_SET_USER`,
`SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL`, the `VMCTL_*` subcalls + prot flags; the five bands
(PM 0x700, VM 0xC00, SEF 0xD00, DS 0xE00, SCHED 0xF00) with their members and
counts; `_Static_assert`s mirroring the Rust `const _` ordering guards.

Two banner notes: (a) MINIX 3's `callnr.h` holds POSIX syscall numbers while ours
holds kernel-call + server-request numbers — a documented deviation; (b)
`NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` is emitted as **`NR_KERN_CALLS`** with a
`/* kernel-shared: NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 */` provenance comment (renaming the Rust
const is nominated for 5.1 — it must be settled before the 5.6 freeze).
**Payload byte offsets are not emitted in 5.0** — they exist only as Rust doc
comments, and D8 says the headers grow as later slices add bands; say so in a
comment, with 5.6's first musl wrapper as the forcing function.

### `minix/errno.h` + the guarded POSIX check

The real hole in "compile it in CI": there is no musl sysroot in 5.0, and a host
`<errno.h>` has **different** values (Darwin `EDEADLK` is 11, `EAGAIN` 35), so
asserting against it would be wrong — or, on glibc, right for the wrong reason.
Three parts:

1. `minix/errno.h` defines **only the MINIX 200-band** (positive magnitudes,
   `<errno.h>` convention; the wire carries them negated) plus always-on
   `_Static_assert(X >= 200)` band guards. The POSIX block is deliberately *not*
   defined — it comes from the C library, which is the whole point of D7.
2. An **opt-in** verification block:
   `#ifdef MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO` → `#include <errno.h>` → 40
   `_Static_assert(EPERM == 1, …)` generated from `error::ALL`. `tools/build-musl.sh`
   (5.6) defines the macro so these fire against the fork's real `bits/errno.h`.
3. A generated **stand-in** `abi-check/errno.h` (40 `#define`s at musl's values from
   the same Rust table, loud "NOT A REAL LIBC HEADER" banner, never installed into
   a sysroot) so CI compiles the guarded block from day one — otherwise a typo like
   `EDEALDK` sits undetected for six slices. Be honest in the plan doc: in 5.0 this
   is a **syntax and name-spelling check**; the value check lands in 5.6.

### `abi-selftest.c`

A header is never a translation unit, so its `_Static_assert`s never fire and
`-fsyntax-only` has nothing to chew on. The selftest is what makes the gate real:
include all four headers **twice** (proves the guards guard), add cross-header
invariants no single header can express (`SCHED_RQ_BASE + NR_SCHED_MSGS - 1 <
NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, `PM_RQ_BASE > KERNEL_CALL + NR_KERN_CALLS - 1`, sentinel
distinctness), and end with a file-scope typedef (ISO C forbids an empty TU).

---

## Part 3 — Host tests for the generator

In-module `#[cfg(test)]` (house style; no crate has a `tests/` dir), inside the
measured lib modules.

**D8's mandated layout snapshot** (`ipc_h.rs`) — asserts the *generated text*
contains `sizeof(message) == {size_of::<Message>()}`, `_Alignof(message) ==
{align_of::<Message>()}` and the payload offset computed by live pointer
arithmetic, plus pins 104/8 directly. This is what stops the generator hardcoding
the numbers and makes a Rust layout change surface in the header or fail here.

negative proc-nrs parenthesized, every process has both macros. `callnr_h` — call

DO-NOT-EDIT on every artifact, all-ASCII, header guards unique, no duplicate
`#define` names within a header, all define names are C identifiers, artifact
paths relative and distinct, and rendering is deterministic.

New **blocking** job `c-headers` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after

headers and cannot accidentally validate against the host libc. No clang install

# Slice 5.0 — errno renumber (D7) + `tools/gen-c-headers` (D8)

## Context

Phase 4 is complete and the pre-Phase-5 cleanup has landed (chunk 6, PR #39, merged
2026-07-24 — `8deaa39`). Phase 5 brings a musl fork and real filesystems, and its
first slice is deliberately **ABI prep before any C exists**:

1. `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` currently carries **bespoke** errno values
   (`EINVAL = -21`, `EFAULT = -15`, `ENOSYS = -44`) behind a comment that wrongly
   claims they "match MINIX 3". musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and its
   `syscall_ret.c` `r > -4096UL` convention only work unmodified if minix.rs
   adopts musl's numbering. Renumbering **now** means no later Phase 5 slice ever
   bakes a soon-to-change errno into a trace marker or a line of C — slice 5.1's
   proof bar already cites `result=-14` (`EFAULT` at its final value).
2. The musl fork needs C headers describing the minix.rs ABI. D8 rejects cbindgen
   (it cannot const-eval the `ProcNr::new()` endpoint constants) in favour of a
   hand-rolled host tool that reads the live Rust constants and prints C. Headers
   are **generated at build time, never committed**, so drift is impossible by
   construction. The ABI freezes at slice 5.6.

Outcome: after this slice the ABI is C-ready, and CI proves the generated headers
compile as C11 on every PR.

Branch: `feature/slice-5.0-abi-prep`. One PR.

---

## Part 1 — `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` rewrite

**Replace the whole file in one write.** `EACCES` is `-14` today and `EFAULT`
becomes `-14`; any incremental edit passes through a state where two live names
alias.

### Shape (decided)

A private declarative macro takes the **positive** musl magnitude and emits both
the negated `pub const` and a derived name/value table:

```rust
macro_rules! errnos {
    ($( $(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident = $magnitude:literal, )*) => {
        $( $(#[$meta])* pub const $name: i32 = -$magnitude; )*
        /// Every errno as `(name, value)` pairs, POSIX block then MINIX band.
        /// Single source of truth for `tools/gen-c-headers`, the band guards,
        /// and the host tests. A `const` (not a `static`) so the kernel — which
        /// never references it — pays nothing in `.rodata`.
        pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)] = &[ $( (stringify!($name), $name), )* ];
    };
}
```

`$(#[$meta:meta])*` captures `///` docs (they desugar to `#[doc]` before matching),
so per-entry rustdoc still works. `$magnitude:literal` (not `:expr`) keeps
`-$magnitude` unambiguous.

### Values

- **POSIX block, magnitudes 1..=40, contiguous** — verified byte-identical between
  `/Users/kevinbarnard/src/learn/rminix/include/errno.h` (classic MINIX) and
  musl's `arch/generic/bits/errno.h`: EPERM 1, ENOENT 2, ESRCH 3, EINTR 4, EIO 5,
  ENXIO 6, E2BIG 7, ENOEXEC 8, EBADF 9, ECHILD 10, EAGAIN 11, ENOMEM 12, EACCES 13,
  EFAULT 14, ENOTBLK 15, EBUSY 16, EEXIST 17, EXDEV 18, ENODEV 19, ENOTDIR 20,
  EISDIR 21, EINVAL 22, ENFILE 23, EMFILE 24, ENOTTY 25, ETXTBSY 26, EFBIG 27,
  ENOSPC 28, ESPIPE 29, EROFS 30, EMLINK 31, EPIPE 32, EDOM 33, ERANGE 34,
  EDEADLK 35, ENAMETOOLONG 36, ENOLCK 37, ENOSYS 38, ENOTEMPTY 39, ELOOP 40.
- **MINIX band, from modern MINIX 3's `sys/sys/errno.h`** — ENOTREADY 201,
  EDEADSRCDST 202, EDONTREPLY 203, EGENERIC 204, ELOCKED 208, EBADCALL 209,
  ECALLDENIED 210, ETRAPDENIED 211, EBADREQUEST 212, and **EBADSRCDST 216** (the
  one name modern MINIX lacks — it spells that condition `EBADEPT` = 216; keep the
  classic name at the modern value and say so in a doc comment).
- Record in the module docs the reserved-but-unadopted 200-band values so nobody
  reuses them: ERESTART 200, EPACKSIZE 205, EURG 206, ENOURG 207, EBADMODE 213,
  ENOCONN 214, EDEADEPT 215, EBADCPU 217.
- `OK = 0` stays, outside `ALL`. Add `POSIX_ERRNO_MAX = 40` and
  `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE = 200`.
- Module doc replaces the wrong "matches MINIX 3" claim with the actual D7 policy.

### Compile-time guards (house `const _: () = …` idiom)

Enforce D7's invariant so nothing can ever land in the 41..=199 gap — the range
where musl defines errnos minix.rs has *not* adopted:

- every value negative; POSIX magnitudes cover 1..=40 exactly once with no holes;
  every other magnitude `>= MINIX_ERRNO_BASE`;
- all values pairwise distinct;
- `OK == 0` (nine sites still spell success as `sef.receive(…) != 0`);
- `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE > POSIX_ERRNO_MAX`.

Const-eval constraints on the pinned nightly: **no iterators/`for`** (use `while` +
`ALL[i]` + `<[T]>::len()`), and **`assert!` messages must be literals** (`assert_eq!`
and `assert!(c, "{x}")` are rejected in const). If slice-indexing `ALL` in a const
block gives trouble, fall back to a `const fn check(t: &[(&str, i32)]) -> ()`.

Keep `ok_is_zero`. Drop `ipc_errors_distinct_from_posix_errors` (subsumed).
Add, all driven off `ALL`: `all_errors_are_negative`, `all_values_distinct`,

tripwire, so a renumber must be a deliberate two-place edit),
`minix_band_matches_modern_minix`, `minix_band_clear_of_musl_range`, and
`table_names_resolve_to_the_named_constants` (proves the macro paired
`stringify!($name)` with the right constant — invisible to every other test).

Use `assert_eq!`, never bare `assert!(CONST op CONST)` inside a `#[test]` — that
trips `assertions_on_constants` under `--all-targets -D warnings`.

### Consumer sweep: zero code changes

Verified: all 27 import sites are symbolic; the only fully-qualified reference is
`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:71` (`minixrs_kernel_shared::error::EINVAL`), still
symbolic. There are **no hardcoded numeric errno literals anywhere** — every

touch five server `main.rs` files and would force a QEMU re-verify for no ABI

```

`define_dec`, `define_hex`, `define_ep`, `static_assert`, `finish`. Two rules that
get their own tests: `define_dec` must parenthesize negatives (`(-2)`, or
`x-SYSTEM_PROC_NR` mis-parses), and all output must stay **ASCII** (no em dashes
leaking into a header that ships into musl).

Use `push_str` + `format!("{name}")`; not `fmt::Write` (`write!` into a `String`
returns a `Result` clippy makes you handle) and never `format!("{}", x)`
(`uninlined_format_args` is default-on).

### `minix/ipc.h`

C11 **keywords**, not GNU attributes: `_Alignas` / `_Alignof` / `_Static_assert`
are guaranteed under `-std=c11 -pedantic-errors`; `__attribute__((aligned))` is not.
Only include is `<stddef.h>` for `offsetof` (a freestanding header, C11 §4p6, so it
survives `-nostdlibinc`).

- `typedef int endpoint_t;` + `_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, …)`.
- `ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT 15`, `ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK 0x7fff`,

  deliberate deviation from MINIX 3's offset bias) — documented in a block comment.
- `struct message` with `_Alignas(8)` on the **first member** (C11 forbids an
  alignment specifier on a struct type declaration; member alignment yields
  `_Alignof(message) == 8`), then `_Static_assert`s pinning sizeof 104, alignof 8,
  and the three member offsets — every number `format!`ed from
  `size_of::<Message>()` / `align_of::<Message>()` / live pointer arithmetic,
  **never typed in**.
- IPC primitives SEND..NOTIFY_MESSAGE.
- Emits **no claim about which register carries the primitive number** —
  `ipc_const.rs:3`'s "`r1`/`x16`" is wrong (it is `x1`), and the plan assigns that
  fix to 5.1; cite the module instead of repeating the claim.

### `minix/com.h`

Includes `<minix/ipc.h>`. `NR_TASKS/NR_PROCS/NR_SYS_PROCS/NR_BOOT_PROCS`,
`ANY/NONE/SELF` cast to `endpoint_t`, `OK`, `EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR`.

Every process gets **two** macros with a block comment explaining they are not
interchangeable: `<NAME>_PROC_NR` (table slot, negative for tasks) and
`<NAME>_EP` (boot endpoint — what belongs in an IPC call). They differ for tasks
because of the sign-extension. `_EP` values come from calling `com::boot_endpoint(nr)`
in the generator (no such Rust const exists; deriving it is exactly the tool's job).
Then `_Static_assert`s validating the hand-written C decode against the
Rust-computed constants — the best value-per-line in the slice:

```c
_Static_assert(SYSTEM_EP == _ENDPOINT(0, SYSTEM_PROC_NR), "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(SYSTEM_EP) == SYSTEM_PROC_NR,  "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(HARDWARE_EP) == HARDWARE_PROC_NR, "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(PM_EP) == PM_PROC_NR, "…");
```

Deliberate omissions, each with a one-line comment so the choice is visible:
stub proc-nrs (`boot-stubs`-scoped, no C consumer), `NR_SERVED_PROCS`,
`USER_VA_TOP`, `sys_limits::*`, and signal numbers (musl's `<signal.h>` is
authoritative and already agrees).

### `minix/callnr.h`

`KERNEL_CALL 0x600` + `SYS_GETINFO`..`SYS_ENDKSIG` (0x600–0x611); `NR_SYS_CALLS 32`;
`GET_WHOAMI`, `SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN`, `EXEC_NAME_LEN`, `PRIVCTL_SET_USER`,
`SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL`, the `VMCTL_*` subcalls + prot flags; the five bands
(PM 0x700, VM 0xC00, SEF 0xD00, DS 0xE00, SCHED 0xF00) with their members and
counts; `_Static_assert`s mirroring the Rust `const _` ordering guards.

Two banner notes: (a) MINIX 3's `callnr.h` holds POSIX syscall numbers while ours
holds kernel-call + server-request numbers — a documented deviation; (b)
`NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` is emitted as **`NR_KERN_CALLS`** with a
`/* kernel-shared: NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 */` provenance comment (renaming the Rust
const is nominated for 5.1 — it must be settled before the 5.6 freeze).
**Payload byte offsets are not emitted in 5.0** — they exist only as Rust doc
comments, and D8 says the headers grow as later slices add bands; say so in a
comment, with 5.6's first musl wrapper as the forcing function.

### `minix/errno.h` + the guarded POSIX check

The real hole in "compile it in CI": there is no musl sysroot in 5.0, and a host
`<errno.h>` has **different** values (Darwin `EDEADLK` is 11, `EAGAIN` 35), so
asserting against it would be wrong — or, on glibc, right for the wrong reason.
Three parts:

1. `minix/errno.h` defines **only the MINIX 200-band** (positive magnitudes,
   `<errno.h>` convention; the wire carries them negated) plus always-on
   `_Static_assert(X >= 200)` band guards. The POSIX block is deliberately *not*
   defined — it comes from the C library, which is the whole point of D7.
2. An **opt-in** verification block:
   `#ifdef MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO` → `#include <errno.h>` → 40
   `_Static_assert(EPERM == 1, …)` generated from `error::ALL`. `tools/build-musl.sh`
   (5.6) defines the macro so these fire against the fork's real `bits/errno.h`.
3. A generated **stand-in** `abi-check/errno.h` (40 `#define`s at musl's values from
   the same Rust table, loud "NOT A REAL LIBC HEADER" banner, never installed into
   a sysroot) so CI compiles the guarded block from day one — otherwise a typo like
   `EDEALDK` sits undetected for six slices. Be honest in the plan doc: in 5.0 this
   is a **syntax and name-spelling check**; the value check lands in 5.6.

### `abi-selftest.c`

A header is never a translation unit, so its `_Static_assert`s never fire and
`-fsyntax-only` has nothing to chew on. The selftest is what makes the gate real:
include all four headers **twice** (proves the guards guard), add cross-header
invariants no single header can express (`SCHED_RQ_BASE + NR_SCHED_MSGS - 1 <
NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, `PM_RQ_BASE > KERNEL_CALL + NR_KERN_CALLS - 1`, sentinel
distinctness), and end with a file-scope typedef (ISO C forbids an empty TU).

In-module `#[cfg(test)]` (house style; no crate has a `tests/` dir), inside the

### Shape (decided)

A private declarative macro takes the **positive** musl magnitude and emits both
the negated `pub const` and a derived name/value table:

```rust
macro_rules! errnos {
    ($( $(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident = $magnitude:literal, )*) => {
        $( $(#[$meta])* pub const $name: i32 = -$magnitude; )*
        /// Every errno as `(name, value)` pairs, POSIX block then MINIX band.
        /// Single source of truth for `tools/gen-c-headers`, the band guards,
        /// and the host tests. A `const` (not a `static`) so the kernel — which
        /// never references it — pays nothing in `.rodata`.
        pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)] = &[ $( (stringify!($name), $name), )* ];
    };

```

`$(#[$meta:meta])*` captures `///` docs (they desugar to `#[doc]` before matching),

2. The musl fork needs C headers describing the minix.rs ABI. D8 rejects cbindgen
   (it cannot const-eval the `ProcNr::new()` endpoint constants) in favour of a
   hand-rolled host tool that reads the live Rust constants and prints C. Headers
   are **generated at build time, never committed**, so drift is impossible by
   construction. The ABI freezes at slice 5.6.

Outcome: after this slice the ABI is C-ready, and CI proves the generated headers
compile as C11 on every PR.

Branch: `feature/slice-5.0-abi-prep`. One PR.

---

## Part 1 — `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` rewrite

**Replace the whole file in one write.** `EACCES` is `-14` today and `EFAULT`
becomes `-14`; any incremental edit passes through a state where two live names
alias.

### Shape (decided)

A private declarative macro takes the **positive** musl magnitude and emits both
the negated `pub const` and a derived name/value table:

```rust
macro_rules! errnos {
    ($( $(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident = $magnitude:literal, )*) => {
        $( $(#[$meta])* pub const $name: i32 = -$magnitude; )*
        /// Every errno as `(name, value)` pairs, POSIX block then MINIX band.
        /// Single source of truth for `tools/gen-c-headers`, the band guards,
        /// and the host tests. A `const` (not a `static`) so the kernel — which
        /// never references it — pays nothing in `.rodata`.
        pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)] = &[ $( (stringify!($name), $name), )* ];
    };
}
```

`$(#[$meta:meta])*` captures `///` docs (they desugar to `#[doc]` before matching),
so per-entry rustdoc still works. `$magnitude:literal` (not `:expr`) keeps
`-$magnitude` unambiguous.

### Values

- **POSIX block, magnitudes 1..=40, contiguous** — verified byte-identical between
  `/Users/kevinbarnard/src/learn/rminix/include/errno.h` (classic MINIX) and
  musl's `arch/generic/bits/errno.h`: EPERM 1, ENOENT 2, ESRCH 3, EINTR 4, EIO 5,
  ENXIO 6, E2BIG 7, ENOEXEC 8, EBADF 9, ECHILD 10, EAGAIN 11, ENOMEM 12, EACCES 13,
  EFAULT 14, ENOTBLK 15, EBUSY 16, EEXIST 17, EXDEV 18, ENODEV 19, ENOTDIR 20,
  EISDIR 21, EINVAL 22, ENFILE 23, EMFILE 24, ENOTTY 25, ETXTBSY 26, EFBIG 27,
  ENOSPC 28, ESPIPE 29, EROFS 30, EMLINK 31, EPIPE 32, EDOM 33, ERANGE 34,
  EDEADLK 35, ENAMETOOLONG 36, ENOLCK 37, ENOSYS 38, ENOTEMPTY 39, ELOOP 40.
- **MINIX band, from modern MINIX 3's `sys/sys/errno.h`** — ENOTREADY 201,
  EDEADSRCDST 202, EDONTREPLY 203, EGENERIC 204, ELOCKED 208, EBADCALL 209,
  ECALLDENIED 210, ETRAPDENIED 211, EBADREQUEST 212, and **EBADSRCDST 216** (the
  one name modern MINIX lacks — it spells that condition `EBADEPT` = 216; keep the
  classic name at the modern value and say so in a doc comment).
- Record in the module docs the reserved-but-unadopted 200-band values so nobody
  reuses them: ERESTART 200, EPACKSIZE 205, EURG 206, ENOURG 207, EBADMODE 213,
  ENOCONN 214, EDEADEPT 215, EBADCPU 217.
- `OK = 0` stays, outside `ALL`. Add `POSIX_ERRNO_MAX = 40` and
  `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE = 200`.
- Module doc replaces the wrong "matches MINIX 3" claim with the actual D7 policy.

### Compile-time guards (house `const _: () = …` idiom)

Enforce D7's invariant so nothing can ever land in the 41..=199 gap — the range
where musl defines errnos minix.rs has *not* adopted:

- every value negative; POSIX magnitudes cover 1..=40 exactly once with no holes;
  every other magnitude `>= MINIX_ERRNO_BASE`;
- all values pairwise distinct;
- `OK == 0` (nine sites still spell success as `sef.receive(…) != 0`);
- `MINIX_ERRNO_BASE > POSIX_ERRNO_MAX`.

Const-eval constraints on the pinned nightly: **no iterators/`for`** (use `while` +
`ALL[i]` + `<[T]>::len()`), and **`assert!` messages must be literals** (`assert_eq!`
and `assert!(c, "{x}")` are rejected in const). If slice-indexing `ALL` in a const
block gives trouble, fall back to a `const fn check(t: &[(&str, i32)]) -> ()`.

### Tests

Keep `ok_is_zero`. Drop `ipc_errors_distinct_from_posix_errors` (subsumed).
Add, all driven off `ALL`: `all_errors_are_negative`, `all_values_distinct`,
`posix_block_matches_musl` (against a literally-pinned 40-entry table — the drift
tripwire, so a renumber must be a deliberate two-place edit),
`minix_band_matches_modern_minix`, `minix_band_clear_of_musl_range`, and
`table_names_resolve_to_the_named_constants` (proves the macro paired
`stringify!($name)` with the right constant — invisible to every other test).

Use `assert_eq!`, never bare `assert!(CONST op CONST)` inside a `#[test]` — that
trips `assertions_on_constants` under `--all-targets -D warnings`.

### Consumer sweep: zero code changes

Verified: all 27 import sites are symbolic; the only fully-qualified reference is
`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:71` (`minixrs_kernel_shared::error::EINVAL`), still
symbolic. There are **no hardcoded numeric errno literals anywhere** — every
negative literal in the tree is a ProcNr. `tests/qemu-boot.expected` /
`.forbidden` carry no errno values, so marker churn is zero. `kernel/build.rs`
already watches `kernel-shared/src` recursively, so the nested server ELFs rebuild.

**Do not** drive-by the nine `sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0` → `!= OK` sites: they
touch five server `main.rs` files and would force a QEMU re-verify for no ABI
reason. Nominate for 5.1, which already owns `server-rt`.

---

## Part 2 — `tools/gen-c-headers` (package `minixrs-gen-c-headers`)

First Rust crate under `tools/` and the first host/`std` crate in the workspace.
Lib + thin bin, matching the `servers/ds` shape (`registry.rs` measured,
`main.rs` Sonar-excluded):

```
tools/gen-c-headers/
  Cargo.toml            # literal fields, publish = false, [lib] + [[bin]], zero third-party deps
  src/lib.rs            # #![forbid(unsafe_code)], artifact list, cross-artifact tests
      builder.rs        # CFile writer: banner, guards, #define, _Static_assert
      ipc_h.rs  com_h.rs  callnr_h.rs  errno_h.rs  selftest.rs
      main.rs           # argv + fs I/O only
```

`publish = false` is load-bearing (`release.yml` publishes a hardcoded 5-crate
list). Zero third-party deps keeps `deny.toml`'s license allow-list untouched.

### CLI

`cargo gen-c-headers [OUTDIR]` (default `target/gen-c-headers`), `--stdout` to
concatenate every artifact to stdout (D8's literal "*prints* the headers"; the
eyeball path), `--help`. `main()` returns `ExitCode`. **Determinism rule, stated in
the crate docs:** no timestamps, hostnames, absolute paths or env reads in output —
the same commit must produce byte-identical bytes for the 5.6 sysroot cache.

Output tree:

```
target/gen-c-headers/
  include/minix/{ipc.h, com.h, callnr.h, errno.h}
  abi-check/errno.h      # musl stand-in, CI-only
  abi-selftest.c
```

`tools/build-musl.sh` (5.6) will copy `include/minix` into the sysroot.

### `builder.rs`

Append-only `CFile { out: String }` with `new(title, sources)` (SPDX + copyright +
`GENERATED FILE -- DO NOT EDIT` banner naming the source `.rs` files and
`cargo gen-c-headers`), `guard_open/close`, `section`, `block_comment`, `include`,
`define_dec`, `define_hex`, `define_ep`, `static_assert`, `finish`. Two rules that
get their own tests: `define_dec` must parenthesize negatives (`(-2)`, or
`x-SYSTEM_PROC_NR` mis-parses), and all output must stay **ASCII** (no em dashes
leaking into a header that ships into musl).

Use `push_str` + `format!("{name}")`; not `fmt::Write` (`write!` into a `String`
returns a `Result` clippy makes you handle) and never `format!("{}", x)`
(`uninlined_format_args` is default-on).

### `minix/ipc.h`

C11 **keywords**, not GNU attributes: `_Alignas` / `_Alignof` / `_Static_assert`
are guaranteed under `-std=c11 -pedantic-errors`; `__attribute__((aligned))` is not.
Only include is `<stddef.h>` for `offsetof` (a freestanding header, C11 §4p6, so it
survives `-nostdlibinc`).

- `typedef int endpoint_t;` + `_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, …)`.
- `ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT 15`, `ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK 0x7fff`,
  `ENDPOINT_MAX_GENERATION 65535`, `ENDPOINT_SLOT_TOP 16383`.
- `_ENDPOINT(g,p)` / `_ENDPOINT_G(e)` / `_ENDPOINT_P(e)` mirroring
  `endpoint.rs`, including the **sign-extension from bit 14** (minix.rs's
  deliberate deviation from MINIX 3's offset bias) — documented in a block comment.
- `struct message` with `_Alignas(8)` on the **first member** (C11 forbids an
  alignment specifier on a struct type declaration; member alignment yields
  `_Alignof(message) == 8`), then `_Static_assert`s pinning sizeof 104, alignof 8,
  and the three member offsets — every number `format!`ed from
  `size_of::<Message>()` / `align_of::<Message>()` / live pointer arithmetic,
  **never typed in**.
- IPC primitives SEND..NOTIFY_MESSAGE.
- Emits **no claim about which register carries the primitive number** —
  `ipc_const.rs:3`'s "`r1`/`x16`" is wrong (it is `x1`), and the plan assigns that
  fix to 5.1; cite the module instead of repeating the claim.

### `minix/com.h`

Includes `<minix/ipc.h>`. `NR_TASKS/NR_PROCS/NR_SYS_PROCS/NR_BOOT_PROCS`,
`ANY/NONE/SELF` cast to `endpoint_t`, `OK`, `EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR`.

Every process gets **two** macros with a block comment explaining they are not
interchangeable: `<NAME>_PROC_NR` (table slot, negative for tasks) and
`<NAME>_EP` (boot endpoint — what belongs in an IPC call). They differ for tasks
because of the sign-extension. `_EP` values come from calling `com::boot_endpoint(nr)`
in the generator (no such Rust const exists; deriving it is exactly the tool's job).
Then `_Static_assert`s validating the hand-written C decode against the
Rust-computed constants — the best value-per-line in the slice:

```c
_Static_assert(SYSTEM_EP == _ENDPOINT(0, SYSTEM_PROC_NR), "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(SYSTEM_EP) == SYSTEM_PROC_NR,  "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(HARDWARE_EP) == HARDWARE_PROC_NR, "…");
_Static_assert(_ENDPOINT_P(PM_EP) == PM_PROC_NR, "…");
```

Deliberate omissions, each with a one-line comment so the choice is visible:
stub proc-nrs (`boot-stubs`-scoped, no C consumer), `NR_SERVED_PROCS`,
`USER_VA_TOP`, `sys_limits::*`, and signal numbers (musl's `<signal.h>` is
authoritative and already agrees).

### `minix/callnr.h`

`KERNEL_CALL 0x600` + `SYS_GETINFO`..`SYS_ENDKSIG` (0x600–0x611); `NR_SYS_CALLS 32`;
`GET_WHOAMI`, `SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN`, `EXEC_NAME_LEN`, `PRIVCTL_SET_USER`,
`SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL`, the `VMCTL_*` subcalls + prot flags; the five bands
(PM 0x700, VM 0xC00, SEF 0xD00, DS 0xE00, SCHED 0xF00) with their members and
counts; `_Static_assert`s mirroring the Rust `const _` ordering guards.

Two banner notes: (a) MINIX 3's `callnr.h` holds POSIX syscall numbers while ours
holds kernel-call + server-request numbers — a documented deviation; (b)
`NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` is emitted as **`NR_KERN_CALLS`** with a
`/* kernel-shared: NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 */` provenance comment (renaming the Rust
const is nominated for 5.1 — it must be settled before the 5.6 freeze).
**Payload byte offsets are not emitted in 5.0** — they exist only as Rust doc
comments, and D8 says the headers grow as later slices add bands; say so in a
comment, with 5.6's first musl wrapper as the forcing function.

### `minix/errno.h` + the guarded POSIX check

The real hole in "compile it in CI": there is no musl sysroot in 5.0, and a host
`<errno.h>` has **different** values (Darwin `EDEADLK` is 11, `EAGAIN` 35), so
asserting against it would be wrong — or, on glibc, right for the wrong reason.
Three parts:

1. `minix/errno.h` defines **only the MINIX 200-band** (positive magnitudes,
   `<errno.h>` convention; the wire carries them negated) plus always-on
   `_Static_assert(X >= 200)` band guards. The POSIX block is deliberately *not*
   defined — it comes from the C library, which is the whole point of D7.
2. An **opt-in** verification block:
   `#ifdef MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO` → `#include <errno.h>` → 40
   `_Static_assert(EPERM == 1, …)` generated from `error::ALL`. `tools/build-musl.sh`
   (5.6) defines the macro so these fire against the fork's real `bits/errno.h`.
3. A generated **stand-in** `abi-check/errno.h` (40 `#define`s at musl's values from
   the same Rust table, loud "NOT A REAL LIBC HEADER" banner, never installed into
   a sysroot) so CI compiles the guarded block from day one — otherwise a typo like
   `EDEALDK` sits undetected for six slices. Be honest in the plan doc: in 5.0 this
   is a **syntax and name-spelling check**; the value check lands in 5.6.

### `abi-selftest.c`

A header is never a translation unit, so its `_Static_assert`s never fire and
`-fsyntax-only` has nothing to chew on. The selftest is what makes the gate real:
include all four headers **twice** (proves the guards guard), add cross-header
invariants no single header can express (`SCHED_RQ_BASE + NR_SCHED_MSGS - 1 <
NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, `PM_RQ_BASE > KERNEL_CALL + NR_KERN_CALLS - 1`, sentinel
distinctness), and end with a file-scope typedef (ISO C forbids an empty TU).

---

## Part 3 — Host tests for the generator

In-module `#[cfg(test)]` (house style; no crate has a `tests/` dir), inside the
measured lib modules.

**D8's mandated layout snapshot** (`ipc_h.rs`) — asserts the *generated text*
contains `sizeof(message) == {size_of::<Message>()}`, `_Alignof(message) ==
{align_of::<Message>()}` and the payload offset computed by live pointer
arithmetic, plus pins 104/8 directly. This is what stops the generator hardcoding
the numbers and makes a Rust layout change surface in the header or fail here.

Plus: `com_h` — `_EP` values equal `boot_endpoint(nr)` recomputed in the test,
negative proc-nrs parenthesized, every process has both macros. `callnr_h` — call
numbers and band bases render from the live constants. `errno_h` — MINIX band is
`error::ALL` above the base, POSIX block is asserted-not-defined, stand-in covers
exactly the 40. `builder` — writer mechanics. `lib` (cross-artifact) — SPDX +
DO-NOT-EDIT on every artifact, all-ASCII, header guards unique, no duplicate
`#define` names within a header, all define names are C identifiers, artifact
paths relative and distinct, and rendering is deterministic.

---

## Part 4 — CI

New **blocking** job `c-headers` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after
`clippy-kernel`, using the house host skeleton verbatim (checkout
`@df4cb1c0…# v6.0.3` → `run: rustup show` → `Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b4977…# v2`):

1. `cargo gen-c-headers`
2. `clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only
   -nostdlibinc -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c`,
   run for both the host triple and `--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`
3. the same with `-DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO -Itarget/gen-c-headers/abi-check`
4. `git diff --exit-code && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` — D8's
   never-committed rule, made mechanical

`-nostdlibinc` (not `-nostdinc`) keeps it hermetic while preserving clang's
freestanding resource-dir headers, so the selftest can only see the generated
headers and cannot accidentally validate against the host libc. No clang install
step: `kernel/build.rs` already shells out to bare `clang`, so it is an existing
hard requirement. Every non-obvious choice gets a `#` comment, per house style.

No other job needs changing: `fmt`/`clippy`/`geiger`/`coverage` pick the member up
automatically, `audit`/`deny` see no new deps, `qemu-smoke` markers are unchanged,
and the crate stays off `miri`'s list deliberately (`forbid(unsafe_code)`, pure
`String` building, all FS I/O in `main.rs`).

---

## Part 5 — Config and docs

- **`Cargo.toml`** — add `"tools/gen-c-headers"` to `members`.
- **`.cargo/config.toml`** — `gen-c-headers = "run -p minixrs-gen-c-headers --"`
  with a comment on the never-committed output.
- **`sonar-project.properties`** — add `tools/**/src/main.rs` to
  `sonar.coverage.exclusions` plus a fourth bullet in the existing rationale block
  (host build-tool entry point: argv + file writes, content produced and unit-tested
  in the measured lib modules, end-to-end verified by the `c-headers` job).
- **`docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`** — 5.0 heading → `◀ ready (branch
  feature/slice-5.0-abi-prep, pending merge)`, 5.1 heading → `◀ next`; fix the
  proof line's `cargo run -p gen-c-headers` → `cargo gen-c-headers`; record the
  5.0 errno-check deferral (POSIX values verified against musl only from 5.6).
- **`docs/plan.md`** — same two marker flips; retitle the pre-Phase-5 section
  `(complete)` and flip chunk 6 to `✓ shipped (PR #39, merged 2026-07-24)`.
- **`docs/plans/phase-5-prep.md:143`** — same chunk-6 flip (currently still
  `◀ ready (branch feature/phase-5-plan, pending merge)`, but `8deaa39` merged it).
- **`docs/plans/phase-2-ipc.md:19`** — additive note on the stale "MINIX errno
  values" claim (it is a history file; annotate, don't rewrite).
- **`book/src/build.md:184`** — "Ten jobs" → "Eleven jobs", add the `c-headers`
  row; add `cargo gen-c-headers` / `cargo test -p minixrs-gen-c-headers` to the
  host-test section. `book/src/reference/syscalls.md` — short "Generated C headers"
  subsection. `book/src/reference/minix3-mapping.md` — correct the `error codes`
  row's provenance and note the headers are generated back into C. No new chapter
  in 5.0 — revisit at 5.6.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — "Nine gates" → "Ten gates", `c-headers` added to the blocking
  list ("the other **eight** block"); `cargo gen-c-headers` in the build section;
  one new conventions bullet covering the two-band errno policy + `errnos!` macro +
  `ALL` as single source of truth, the generator's lib+bin shape and
  never-committed rule, C11 keywords over GNU attributes, and `_PROC_NR` vs `_EP`.
  Extend the existing const-guard bullet with the const-eval limits found here
  (literal-only `assert!` messages, no iterators — use `while` + indexing).
  Run `/claude-md-management:revise-claude-md` before opening the PR, per the
  global pre-PR checklist.

---

## Verification

```sh
cargo fmt --all && cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --no-default-features -- -D warnings

cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared      # errno macro, ALL, band + distinctness guards
cargo test -p minixrs-gen-c-headers      # renderers, layout snapshot, cross-artifact rules
cargo test -p minixrs-vm -p minixrs-pm -p minixrs-ds -p minixrs-server-rt

cargo gen-c-headers
for t in "" "--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"; do
  clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only -nostdlibinc $t \
    -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
done
clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only -nostdlibinc \
  -DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO -Itarget/gen-c-headers/abi-check \
  -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all   # must be empty

# QEMU: the real proof the renumber is behaviour-neutral (values changed, markers green).
# `timeout 25` per CLAUDE.md — shorter runs produce a log with no kernel output at all.
cargo kernel-aarch64
timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release \
  > /tmp/qemu-5.0.log 2>&1 || true
tools/check-boot-log.sh /tmp/qemu-5.0.log
timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release \
  --no-default-features > /tmp/qemu-5.0-nostubs.log 2>&1 || true
grep -a "KERNEL PANIC" /tmp/qemu-5.0-nostubs.log   # must be empty
```

---

## Risks

- **Transient errno aliasing** (`EACCES -14` → `EFAULT -14`) — whole-file
  replacement only.
- **Const-eval limits**: literal-only `assert!` messages, no iterators/`for`; if
  slice-indexing `ALL` in a const block misbehaves, move the guards into a
  `const fn` taking `&[(&str, i32)]`.
- **Clippy under `-D warnings --all-targets`**: `assertions_on_constants` inside
  `#[test]` fns, `uninlined_format_args` across a string-heavy generator,
  `doc_lazy_continuation` on the 50 new doc comments.
- **`_Alignas` must sit on a member**, not the struct type — a compile error the
  selftest catches immediately.
- **`-pedantic-errors` is a bet** justified by choosing pure C11 keywords; verify
  locally before making the job blocking, and fall back to `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`
  if anything unexpected fires. `-nostdlibinc` is clang-only — note it in the job
  comment so nobody "portably" swaps in `cc`.
- **Generic C macro names** (`ANY`, `NONE`, `SELF`, `OK`, `SEND`, `NOTIFY`) are
  MINIX-authentic but collision-prone once real musl sources include these headers
  at 5.6; mitigated by suffixing every process name (`SYSTEM_PROC_NR`/`SYSTEM_EP`,
  never bare `SYSTEM`) and casting the sentinels. Watch `NONE`/`SELF` at 5.6.
- **Sonar new-code coverage** on the new lib files — the test suite above is sized
  for that, not just for correctness.

Cleared while planning: no stale server ELFs (`build.rs` watches `kernel-shared/src`
recursively); zero marker churn; `panic = "abort"` does not affect `#[test]`
harnesses (cargo ignores it for the test profile); `target/` is gitignored so the
default OUTDIR satisfies the never-committed rule.

#ifndef _MINIX_IPC_H
#define _MINIX_IPC_H

/*
 * This header deliberately includes nothing in the common case: it
 * describes a kernel ABI and must be usable from freestanding C as well as
 * from musl user space. The one thing it needs is offsetof, which comes
 * from a compiler builtin under a private name -- both to avoid depending
 * on <stddef.h> and to avoid ever colliding with the C library's own
 * offsetof macro.
 *
 * The fallback exists for a hypothetical non-GNU-flavoured compiler; the
 * supported toolchain is clang (phase-5 decision D10).
 */
#if defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
#define _MINIX_OFFSETOF(t, m)    __builtin_offsetof(t, m)
#else
#include <stddef.h>   /* offsetof */
#define _MINIX_OFFSETOF(t, m)    offsetof(t, m)
#endif

/* ---- endpoints ---- */
typedef int endpoint_t;
_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, "the minix.rs ABI assumes a 32-bit int for endpoint_t");

#define ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT       15
#define ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK       0x7fff
#define ENDPOINT_MAX_GENERATION  65535
#define ENDPOINT_SLOT_TOP        16383

#define ANY                      ((endpoint_t) 16383)
#define NONE                     ((endpoint_t) 16382)
#define SELF                     ((endpoint_t) 16381)

/*
 * Endpoint packing. minix.rs deviates from MINIX 3 deliberately: the proc
 * field is SIGN-EXTENDED from bit ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT-1 to recover negative
 * kernel-task slots, rather than MINIX 3's MAX_NR_TASKS offset bias. These
 * mirror endpoint.rs::{make_endpoint, endpoint_proc, endpoint_gen}.
 *
 * The consequence is that _ENDPOINT(0, p) != p for negative p, which is why
 * minix/com.h gives every process both a _PROC_NR and an _EP macro.
 */
#define _ENDPOINT(g, p)  (((g) << ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT) | ((p) & ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK))

c-headers:
    name: generated C headers
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Blocking (phase-5 decision D8): the generated headers are the musl fork's
    # only view of the minix.rs ABI, and they are never committed — so a Rust
    # change that produces uncompilable C has to fail in the slice that made it,
    # not in slice 5.6 when the first C file appears.
    #
    # No clang install step: kernel/build.rs already shells out to bare `clang`
    # to assemble the kernel's .S files, so it is an existing hard build
    # requirement that the runner images satisfy.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - name: Install pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
      - name: Generate headers
        run: cargo gen-c-headers
      # -nostdlibinc (clang-only; do not "portably" swap in cc) plus
      # -ffreestanding keeps the check hermetic: the selftest sees ONLY the
      # generated headers and clang's own resource-dir headers, so it cannot
      # accidentally validate against the host libc — whose errno values differ
      # from musl's (Darwin EDEADLK is 11, not 35). Three triples: the host
      # proves portability, the two musl triples are what actually ships.
      # -fsyntax-only needs no backend, no linker, and no sysroot.
      - name: Syntax-check the generated headers
        run: |
          for target in "" "--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl" \
                           "--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"; do
            clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
              -fsyntax-only -ffreestanding -nostdlibinc $target \
              -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include \
              target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
          done
      # Compiles <minix/errno.h>'s opt-in POSIX block against the generated
      # stand-in. A syntax and macro-spelling check only — the stand-in is
      # generated from the same Rust table the assertions check. The real value
      # check runs against the musl fork's bits/errno.h from slice 5.6 on.
      - name: Syntax-check the opt-in errno assertions
        run: |
          clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
            -fsyntax-only -ffreestanding -nostdlibinc \
            --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl \
            -DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO \
            -Itarget/gen-c-headers/abi-check \
            -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include \
            target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
      # D8: the headers are build artifacts under target/ and are never
      # committed. Makes that rule mechanical rather than a convention.
      - name: Assert nothing was written into the tree
        run: |
          git diff --exit-code
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"

  audit:
    name: cargo-audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # to assemble the kernel's .S files, so it is an existing hard build
    # requirement that the runner images satisfy.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - name: Install pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
      - name: Generate headers
        run: cargo gen-c-headers
      # -nostdlibinc (clang-only; do not "portably" swap in cc) plus
      # -ffreestanding keeps the check hermetic: the selftest sees ONLY the
      # generated headers and clang's own resource-dir headers, so it cannot
      # accidentally validate against the host libc — whose errno values differ
      # from musl's (Darwin EDEADLK is 11, not 35). Three triples: the host
      # proves portability, the two musl triples are what actually ships.
      # -fsyntax-only needs no backend, no linker, and no sysroot.
      - name: Syntax-check the generated headers
        run: |
          for target in "" "--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl" \
                           "--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"; do
            clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
              -fsyntax-only -ffreestanding -nostdlibinc $target \
              -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include \
              target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
          done
      # Compiles <minix/errno.h>'s opt-in POSIX block against the generated
      # stand-in. A syntax and macro-spelling check only — the stand-in is
      # generated from the same Rust table the assertions check. The real value
      # check runs against the musl fork's bits/errno.h from slice 5.6 on.
      - name: Syntax-check the opt-in errno assertions
        run: |
          clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
            -fsyntax-only -ffreestanding -nostdlibinc \
            --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl \
            -DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO \
            -Itarget/gen-c-headers/abi-check \
            -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include \
            target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
      # D8: the headers are build artifacts under target/ and are never
      # committed. Makes that rule mechanical rather than a convention.
      - name: Assert nothing was written into the tree
        run: |
          git diff --exit-code
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"
